reports.title: Mary Jones
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: Mary Jones was a frail elderly lady who was moved from the MRI to Trafford General post-operatively for rehabilitation under the Trust structure. It was a planned transfer. However due to limited transport availability she arrived at Trafford General out of hours after waiting for transfer. As a result she was clerked in and risk assessed out of hours despite the recognised risks of moving frail elderly patients out of hours. concerns.hazard: frail elderly patient transferred out of hours

concerns.quote: The falls risk assessment was completed outside the Trust target time primarily as a result of the late arrival
The documentation within the nursing notes, particularly the fluid charts was poor quality, making it difficult to understand what had happened in relation to the hydration of Mrs Jones

The documentation issue was exacerbated by the Trust IT merger having resulted in the loss of a number of key documents. It was unclear how the Trust were managing the risks around lost medical records where the IT merger was at the root of the issue
concerns.hazard: loss of medical records due to IT merger

concerns.quote: Despite her frailty there was no evidence available at the inquest of a referral to a dietician/nutritionist. There was to have been a referral to SALT in February but no trace could be found of the referral
There was no evidence of clear clinical review of the outcome of the fluid charts
concerns.hazard: lack of clinical review of fluid charts

reports.title: Evelyn Ross
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

promises.quote: The Trust has an established process in place to review nursing workforce establishments and skill mix for all wards. This utilises an evidence-based triangulated approach to determine nurse staffing levels and skill mix, that reflect patient acuity and dependency requirements to inform workforce planning. The Safer Nursing Care Tool (SNCT) is utilised to gather patient acuity and dependency data over a four-week period. Ward 6 completed data collection periods in March, June and September 2019 and
promises.summary: Review nursing staffing using SNCT data to inform workforce planning

concerns.quote: The inquest was told that the ward in question had been short staffed for a number of months. As a result there was a reliance on agency staff and less experienced staff. The trust was now seeking to resolve the issue but it was still not fully resolved. It reflected a wider issue of a national shortage of nurses.
concerns.hazard: staffing shortages leading to reliance on agency and less experienced staff

concerns.quote: The inquest was told that whilst Mrs Ross was medically fit for discharge prior to 1st July she had not been discharged because of delays in arranging a suitable care package to support her in the community.
concerns.hazard: delayed discharge due to lack of community care package

concerns.quote: During the course of the inquest the documentation relied on by the trust was lacking in detail and meant that it was difficult to understand her condition at key points or to understand the rationale for decisions.
concerns.hazard: inadequate documentation of patient condition and decisions

concerns.quote: The inquest heard that the Trust had not followed their own falls risk policy in relation to Mrs Ross.

There did not appear to be a clear system of regular orthogeriatric consultant reviews of Mrs Ross. This meant that there was no escalation of her condition to a consultant when she began to show signs of deterioration.
concerns.hazard: absence of regular orthogeriatric consultant reviews

reports.title: Janet Anderson: Prevention of Future Deaths Report
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: The inquest heard evidence that the prolonged hospital stay and lack of progress in finding a suitable place in the community significantly contributed to her decline
The GMMH documentation was of a poor quality and did not capture key discussions/decisions including in relation to medication
The lack of progress in discharge meant that an acute hospital bed was not available to other patients who needed care in an acute setting
